title: Viva Engage: tenant-wide custom branding from a Brand center in the Engage admin center
summary: The branding behaviour, licensing, roadmap facts and documented controls are supported by Microsoft's sources. Minor corrections should distinguish optional branding from automatic personal-theme retirement, complete the theme-control guidance and clarify the role-assignment API.

claims.where: What's changing; title; summary; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Engage-level administrators can configure a tenant-wide brand name, large and small logos and theme colour.
claims.quote: Engage-level admins can configure a brand name, add large and small logos, and a theme color that is applied consistently for all users in the tenant.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; title; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Brand center in the Viva Engage admin center is the location for configuring and publishing branding.
claims.quote: It's configured from a new Brand center in the Viva Engage admin center, and nothing changes for users in the tenant until an admin publishes it.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Custom branding is administrator opt-in and branding changes do not reach users until published.
claims.quote: It's configured from a new Brand center in the Viva Engage admin center, and nothing changes for users in the tenant until an admin publishes it.

claims.claim: Branding applies on Engage web, the Engage app in Teams and the iOS and Android mobile apps.
claims.quote: Custom Branding is an admin-managed capability that applies a tenant-wide brand name, logos, and theme color across Viva Engage on the web, Engage app in Teams, and in the iOS and Android mobile apps.

claims.claim: Administrators can pick a colour from the existing theme palette.
claims.quote: Pick from the existing theme palette or add your own hex value with the + under Themes.

claims.claim: Administrators can supply their own hex colour value.
claims.quote: Pick from the existing theme palette or add your own hex value with the + under Themes.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Administrators can preview branding on web, mobile and the Engage app in Teams before publishing.
claims.quote: Preview before you publish — See exactly how your branding will look before anyone else does, on all platforms - Web, Mobile, Engage app in Teams.

claims.claim: Discarding unpublished changes returns to the last published branding version.
claims.quote: When it's right, publish it to the organization. If it doesn't look right, discard changes to go back to the last published version.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[0]
claims.claim: This release provides one brand name, logo set and theme colour for the entire tenant, rather than separate divisional branding.
claims.quote: Custom Branding is tenant-wide in this release — one brand name, logo set, and theme color across the entire network.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[2].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Published Engage branding takes precedence over the Microsoft 365 organisation theme inside Engage.
claims.quote: Simply said, Branding set in Engage always has higher priority than M365 organizational theme, and wins in the case that both are applied.

claims.claim: Before Engage branding is published, the Microsoft 365 organisation theme's navigation bar colour applies to the Engage web header.
claims.quote: if an organizational theme was applied in a tenant (and no branding has been published), the navigation bar color will continue to be applied to the Engage web header

claims.claim: Before Engage branding is published, the Microsoft 365 organisation theme's accent colour applies to Engage web buttons and links.
claims.quote: the Accent color will be applied to components such as buttons and links in the Web app.

claims.claim: Without Engage branding or a Microsoft 365 organisation theme, users see the default Engage experience.
claims.quote: If Branding is not set in Engage, then we attempt to pick the org theme set in M365 admin center. If the tenant has no M365 org theme either, then the users in that tenant see the default Engage experience.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Scope; controls[1]; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Engage Administrator role is called Yammer administrator in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: Engage Administrator | Configures and manages all aspects of Viva Engage including tenant settings, core and premium features, badges enablement, and compliance. This role is also referred to as Yammer administrator in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: Scope; Risk assessment; controls[1].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The announcement restricts branding setup to a Viva Engage administrator with Engage admin center access.
claims.quote: Only a Viva Engage administrator that can has access to the Engage admin center can set up Branding. Branding is applied to users only once an admin publishes it for the tenant.

claims.claim: The Entra role-assignment route is Identity > Roles & admins > role > Add assignments.
claims.quote: Browse to Identity > Roles & admins. Select a role name to open the role. Don't add a check mark next to the role. Select Add assignments and then select the users, groups, or agent identities you want to assign to this role.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments assigns an Entra directory role.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments
{
    "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.unifiedRoleAssignment",
    "principalId": "<Object ID of user or group>",
    "roleDefinitionId": "<ID of role definition>",
    "directoryScopeId": "/"
}
claims.fix: Keep the call unchanged. Add to controls[1].note: 'The request body sets roleDefinitionId to the Yammer Administrator role definition, principalId to the assignee, and directoryScopeId to / for tenant scope.' The cited Entra role-assignment page documents these properties.

claims.claim: Assigning the Yammer Administrator role requires at least Privileged Role Administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a Privileged Role Administrator.
claims.fix: Keep the Entra requirement, but add: 'The Engage administrator-role page lists a Microsoft 365 Global administrator under Who can assign, whereas the Entra tenant-role assignment guide requires at least Privileged Role Administrator.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/engage/eac-key-admin-roles-permissions and https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/manage-roles-portal.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 organisation themes are reached through Settings > Org Settings > Organization profile > Custom themes.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Settings > Org Settings page, and then choose the Organization profile tab. On the Organization profile tab, select Custom themes.
claims.fix: The printed path correctly reaches the theme list. For the colour-setting control, extend controls[2].ui.path to 'Settings > Org Settings > Organization profile > Custom themes > Default Theme > Colors'. The cited page says to select Default Theme and documents Navigation bar color and Accent color on Colors. The checklist's inspection path can remain unchanged.

claims.claim: Only Global Administrators can customise Microsoft 365 organisation themes.
claims.quote: Only global admins can customize company themes. Global readers have read-only access.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 themes recommend a 4.5:1 contrast ratio.
claims.quote: The recommended contrast ratio between text, icon or button color and background color is 4.5:1. You can override this recommendation and still save your theme as this is not a requirement.

claims.claim: The Viva Engage app's name can be customised through the Teams app store.
claims.quote: From the Teams app store, you can customize the appearance for the following Viva Engage properties: app name; app description; app icons; accent color.

claims.claim: The Viva Engage app's accent colour can be customised through the Teams app store.
claims.quote: From the Teams app store, you can customize the appearance for the following Viva Engage properties: app name; app description; app icons; accent color.

claims.claim: Teams-store app customisations do not change branding inside the Engage experience.
claims.quote: Currently, customizations don't affect the Viva Engage app branding that appears within the Viva Engage experience.

claims.claim: The Engage admin center is reached from Viva Engage through Settings > Admin center.
claims.quote: In Viva Engage, select Settings > Admin center.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph's Viva Engage API covers communities, roles and user following.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Graph API enables apps to manage communities and roles in Viva Engage. Viva Engage supports user following functionality that enables employees to connect with colleagues and stay updated on their activities within the platform.

claims.claim: No branding-setting or publishing API is documented, including in the Viva Engage Microsoft Graph API.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage custom branding publish theme API Microsoft Graph Yammer REST PowerShell. Read Graph Engage overview (beta) and Yammer Core APIs; neither lists a branding operation. Search results describe messages, users, communities and roles.

claims.claim: No API for the Microsoft 365 suite-header organisation theme is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 organization custom themes suite header PowerShell Microsoft Graph API; Microsoft 365 Custom themes API navigation. Read customize-your-organization-theme and Graph organizationalBrandingTheme (beta); the latter configures sign-in pages, not suite-header themes.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly stated whether the Network Administrator or Verified Administrator roles can publish the new branding.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage custom branding Brand center Microsoft Learn navigation publish network verified administrator. Read announcement FAQ, Engage admin roles and tenant settings. The FAQ does not explicitly name Network or Verified roles for branding.

claims.claim: Engage tenant settings have an existing Tenant logo setting.
claims.quote: Tenant logo | An Engage admin, network admin, or verified admin can upload the organization's logo to the Viva Engage tenant.

claims.claim: The existing Tenant logo appears on users' home feeds.
claims.quote: The logo appears on every user’s home feed and on the Leadership corner header.

claims.claim: The existing Tenant logo appears on the Leadership corner header.
claims.quote: The logo appears on every user’s home feed and on the Leadership corner header.

claims.claim: A specific audit event for publishing or discarding custom branding is not established by the documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage custom branding audit publish; Viva Engage activities branding theme. Read announcement and Learn search excerpts from track-engage-events and audit-log-activities; results document other network-setting events, not branding publish/discard events.

claims.claim: Brand center logo-file limits are not yet documented in a Microsoft Learn guide.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage Brand center logo limit; Viva Engage Brand center navigation. Read announcement, setup and tenant configuration pages; results cover tenant-logo and unrelated branding limits, not Brand center logo-file limits.

claims.claim: Branding is shown in light and dark modes on mobile.
claims.quote:
Branded Engage mobile app in light mode
Branded Engage mobile app in dark mode

claims.where: front matter: action; Why it matters
claims.claim: The action rating review treats the entire described change as optional despite automatic personal-theme retirement.
claims.quote:
action: "review"
The change users will notice regardless is the retirement of personal user themes, which the announcement suggests telling users about.
claims.fix: Set action to 'prepare': the briefing includes a user-theme retirement that arrives without administrator publishing and calls for communications. Keep defaultState as 'admin-opt-in' for the custom-branding control.

claims.claim: Impact is medium even though the rationale describes a tenant-wide change visible to every Engage user.
claims.quote:
impact: "medium"
impact: Medium. Once published, every Engage user sees the brand on web, Teams and mobile, and users who chose a personal theme lose it as user themes are retired.
claims.fix: Set impact to 'high' and replace the rationale with 'High. Once published, every Engage user sees the brand on web, Teams and mobile; personal user themes are also retired with the rollout.' This matches the scale's most-users definition.
